results.title: SKI: the voice-first coding harness for your Mac
results.content:
The wrong instruction runs

"Delete the test file" / "delete the rest of the file." A misheard word executes.

What's inside

## One harness for every agent, every project, every language.

Talk to it, hear it talk back, and let it run the rest, on any model, with git built in.

Hands-free voice

Talk to your agents. Hear them talk back.

Real-time talkback while you pace, sketch or make coffee. Ask for a change, hear what happened, answer the next question, without going back to the keyboard.

You talkIt talks backNo keyboard needed

A developer stands by the window with a coffee and headphones, away from the laptop, while SKI reads back the result

SKIski · vega

Tests pass. The menu fix is on vega. Want me to open the PR?

"Yes, open it."

Multilingual [...] Acknowledgement is separate from the answer

A reply is expected in ~200 ms; an agent turn runs ~45 s. A fast layer holds the conversation while the slow work runs.

The prompt is missing

You type composed prompts. You speak messy ones. The harness works out the intent and asks instead of guessing.

It assumes it will be misheard

Repair is designed in from the start, not bolted on after a bad transcription.

None of this can be retrofitted with a microphone.

Security

## Your code stays on your Mac.

Your projects, code and chats stay on your Mac, and your agents run on your own accounts. Your voice goes through the cloud to be understood and answered. It isn't stored.

Code stays on your Mac Your own agent accounts Voice not stored Irreversible steps ask first [...] Git built in, from branch to pull request.

Every chat gets its own branch and worktree, so agents never step on each other. Watch the diff as it happens, then say "open the PR".

results.content:
Voice coding for your agent

# Let your coding agent talk with you.

You talk. It builds. It answers — out loud, in a natural voice. Everything runs on your own computer; nothing you say ever leaves it. Free for life.

Download See how it works

macOS Windows Linux

SKI - Free voice coding for Claude Code, Codex and more | Product Hunt

SKIFileEditViewWindowHelp Fri 10:09

Run the tests and tell me what broke.

Two failures in auth.test.ts — the new token refresh.

recipes~/recipes

Speech-to-text and the voice both run on your computer.

0

Bytes uploaded

Your audio and transcripts are never sent to us.

∞

Recording retention

Meeting recordings stay on your disk for as long as you keep them.

6+

Agents supported

Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, Gemini CLI, OpenClaw and more. [...] Do I have to keep the mic on the whole time?

No — mute it any time and SKI stops listening and releases the mic. On Mac you can also use the globe / fn key: tap to mute or unmute, or hold it as push-to-talk (Mac only; opt-in, needs one macOS permission).

 How is this different from other voice tools?

Most are speech-to-text dictation — they put your words in a box and stop. SKI is a two-way voice loop for coding agents: it answers out loud, and it shows you what your agent is doing. Different job.

 Do I need an internet connection?

No. Listening, understanding, and speaking all happen on your own machine. The only feature that touches the internet is sending your agent into a video meeting — and that's optional.

 Is my voice recorded or sent anywhere? [...] A / Local models

### Hears and speaks on your machine

Speech recognition and a natural neural voice, both running on-device. No audio is ever uploaded — there is nothing to upload it to.

B / Nothing hidden

### No daemon, no cloud

The widget and your agent talk through plain files inside your own project. Inspect every byte; delete them any time.

C / You approve

### Approve-before-send

Optional review mode: every transcript lands in an editable bubble first. Nothing reaches the agent until you hit ✓.

Now in the notch

## It lives in your notch.

Very promising approach - two things which made me uninstall it after a few minutes:   
  
a) I need a way to select input and output. I have multiple mics (Jabra wireless headset for meetings, Rode mic for video recordings, some system loops etc) and also multiple outputs. (When it gets late I want that output on my headset to not annoy my family)  
  
b) price intransparency. I understand that you need to make money. We all do. But if you tell me "free for lifetime" then I am annoyed if I see $2.50 somewhere in the fineprint of my account status. Be open about your pricing. You are competing against other tools that I pay for and I am happy to pay for a better tool
